lem-it-weighted-centroid-squared-error-i:
## Statement

Let $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in\mathbb R^d$, let $w_i>0$ with $\sum_{i=1}^Nw_i=1$, and let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ be nonempty. Put $W_S:=\sum_{i\in S}w_i$ and $\mu_S:=W_S^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}w_ix_i$. For every $c\in\mathbb R^d$,

$$\sum_{i\in S}w_i\|x_i-c\|_2^2=\sum_{i\in S}w_i\|x_i-\mu_S\|_2^2+W_S\|c-\mu_S\|_2^2.$$

Consequently, $\mu_S$ is the unique minimizer of the cluster's weighted squared error. If $S$ is empty, its cost is zero for every center and no centroid is required.
def-it-point-density-cumulative-map:
## Definition

Let $a<b$ and let $g:[a,b]\to(0,\infty)$ be a continuously differentiable function with $\int_a^b g(t)\,dt=1$. Its cumulative point-density coordinate is

$$G_g(x):=\int_a^x g(t)\,dt,\qquad x\in[a,b].$$

The integrals here are the ordinary Riemann integrals of continuous functions. The supplier [[cor-primitives-of-a-continuous-function]] guarantees that they are defined and that $G_g$ is a primitive of $g$.
def-it-finite-squared-error-quantizer:
## Definition

Let $d,k\ge1$, let $X\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be Borel, and give $X$ the relative Borel sigma algebra $\mathcal B(X)=\{X\cap B:B\text{ is in the sigma algebra generated by Euclidean open sets in }\mathbb R^d\}$. Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathcal B(X)$ with $\int_X\|x\|_2^2\,d\mu(x)<\infty$, and let $c_1,\ldots,c_k\in\mathbb R^d$ be reproduction points, where $\|x\|_2^2:=\sum_{\ell=1}^d x_\ell^2$. A finite squared-error quantizer is a measurable map $Q:X\to\{1,\ldots,k\}$, with the finite index set given its discrete sigma algebra; its reproduction at $x$ is $c_{Q(x)}$ and its distortion is

$$D_\mu(Q;c_1,\ldots,c_k):=\int_X\|x-c_{Q(x)}\|_2^2\,d\mu(x).$$

This is the expected single-letter distortion of [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]] for the measurable distortion $d(x,c)=\|x-c\|_2^2$. For a fixed ordered center tuple $c=(c_1,\ldots,c_k)$, the nearest-center rule assigns $x$ to the least index minimizing $\|x-c_j\|_2^2$. Its cell at index $i$ is

$$C_i(c):=X\cap\bigcap_{j<i}\{x:\|x-c_i\|_2^2<\|x-c_j\|_2^2\}\cap\bigcap_{j>i}\{x:\|x-c_i\|_2^2\le\|x-c_j\|_2^2\}.$$

The convention assigns every tie to the smallest index. A general finite measurable quantizer need not use this nearest-center partition; in particular, a compander partition below is specified by its own interval boundaries. When $X=\mathbb R^d$, this is the ordinary full-domain nearest-center quantizer.
lem-it-point-density-cumulative-map-is-c:
## Statement

Let $a<b$ and let $g:[a,b]\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$ with $\int_a^b g=1$, and let $G_g$ be as in [[def-it-point-density-cumulative-map]]. Then $G_g$ is a strictly increasing $C^2$ bijection from $[a,b]$ onto $[0,1]$. Its inverse $\phi:[0,1]\to[a,b]$ is $C^2$ (with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints), and

$$\phi'(u)=\frac{1}{g(\phi(u))},\qquad \phi''(u)=-\frac{g'(\phi(u))}{g(\phi(u))^3}.$$
lem-it-nearest-center-quantizer-is-borel:
## Statement

Let $X\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be Borel, let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $X$ with finite second moment, and let $c_1,\ldots,c_k\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfy the hypotheses of [[def-it-finite-squared-error-quantizer]]. The least-index nearest-center rule defines a Borel quantizer on $X$, and its distortion is finite. Coincident centers and empty cells are allowed.
def-it-compact-one-dimensional-compander:
## Definition

Let $a<b$. Let $f,g:[a,b]\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$ probability densities, so $\int_a^bf=\int_a^bg=1$. Write $G_g$ for [[def-it-point-density-cumulative-map]] and $\phi=G_g^{-1}$ for the $C^2$ inverse established by [[lem-it-point-density-cumulative-map-is-c2-diffeomorphism]]. For each integer $N\ge1$, define boundaries

$$\beta_j:=\phi(j/N)\quad(0\le j\le N),$$

and reproduction points

$$r_j:=\phi((j-\tfrac12)/N)\quad(1\le j\le N).$$

The cells are $[\beta_{j-1},\beta_j)$ for $j<N$ and $[\beta_{N-1},b]$ for $j=N$. The compander quantizer maps every point in cell $j$ to $r_j$. It is a finite measurable quantizer in the sense of [[def-it-finite-squared-error-quantizer]], with source law of density $f$ on $[a,b]$ and squared-error distortion

$$D_N(f,g):=\sum_{j=1}^N\int_{\beta_{j-1}}^{\beta_j}f(x)(x-r_j)^2\,dx.$$

Its cells are uniform in the cumulative coordinate of $g$; the definition does not assert that they are nearest-center cells in the original $x$ coordinate. Since the source is supported on the fixed compact interval and the cells cover it, there is no overload region in this model.
alg-it-finite-data-lloyd-quantizer:
## Definition

Input: integers $N,d,k\ge1$, indexed data $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in\mathbb R^d$, exact positive weights $w_i$ with $\sum_iw_i=1$, and an ordered initial center tuple $c^0=(c_1^0,\ldots,c_k^0)\in(\mathbb R^d)^k$. At each pass $t$:

1. Assign index $i$ to the least $j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$ minimizing $\|x_i-c_j^t\|_2^2$. Let $S_j^t$ be the indices assigned to $j$.
2. If $S_j^t\ne\varnothing$, set $c_j^{t+1}:=(\sum_{i\in S_j^t}w_ix_i)/(\sum_{i\in S_j^t}w_i)$. If $S_j^t=\varnothing$, set $c_j^{t+1}:=c_j^t$.
3. If $c^{t+1}=c^t$ coordinatewise, return $c^t$ and the assignments from this pass. Otherwise begin the next pass with $c^{t+1}$.

All distance comparisons and arithmetic are exact. Rational input coordinates, weights and initial centers give a rational implementation using exact rational operations. For arbitrary real data this is an exact-real operation model; no bit-complexity claim is part of the procedure.
alg-it-exhaustive-global-empirical-quant:
## Definition

Input: integers $N,d,k\ge1$, indexed data $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in\mathbb R^d$, and exact positive weights $w_i$ with $\sum_iw_i=1$. Enumerate all assignments $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_N)\in\{1,\ldots,k\}^N$ in lexicographic order. For each assignment, let $S_j(a)=\{i:a_i=j\}$. For a nonempty $S_j(a)$ set

$$c_j(a):=\frac{\sum_{i\in S_j(a)}w_ix_i}{\sum_{i\in S_j(a)}w_i};$$

for an empty $S_j(a)$ set $c_j(a):=x_1$. Compute the exact assigned cost $L(a):=\sum_iw_i\|x_i-c_{a_i}(a)\|_2^2$. Retain the first assignment with minimal cost and its center tuple. Return that tuple together with the least-index nearest-center assignment for it. The finite enumeration, tie rule and empty-cluster convention are part of the algorithm.
lem-it-compact-compander-quantizer-is-bo:
## Statement

For the data in [[def-it-compact-one-dimensional-compander]], every cell is Borel, the cells partition $[a,b]$, the index map is measurable, and $D_N(f,g)$ is finite for each $N\ge1$.
thm-it-finite-data-lloyd-termination-and:
## Statement

For $N$ indexed points in $\mathbb R^d$ with positive normalized weights, $k\ge1$ centers, and any initial center tuple, the exact algorithm of [[alg-it-finite-data-lloyd-quantizer]] terminates after at most $2^{Nk}$ assignment/update passes. Every pass that changes a center strictly decreases the empirical squared-error distortion; at termination, the returned assignment is nearest-center and each nonempty cluster center is its weighted centroid. Each pass uses $O(Nkd)$ exact arithmetic and comparisons, so the crude total operation bound is $O(2^{Nk}Nkd)$. The conclusion is a fixed point, not a global-optimality claim.
thm-it-exhaustive-global-empirical-quant:
## Statement

For every finite indexed data set $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in\mathbb R^d$ with $N,d,k\ge1$ and positive normalized weights, the algorithm of [[alg-it-exhaustive-global-empirical-quantizer]] terminates after checking exactly $k^N$ assignments and returns a nearest-center quantizer whose empirical squared-error distortion is no greater than that of any $k$-center tuple. Its exact arithmetic operation count is $O(k^N(N+k)d)$; this is an exponential exhaustive procedure, not a polynomial-time claim.
thm-it-compact-compander-high-rate-disto:
## Statement

Let $a<b$ and let $f,g:[a,b]\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$ probability densities. For the compander of [[def-it-compact-one-dimensional-compander]], the distortions satisfy

$$\lim_{N\to\infty}N^2D_N(f,g)=\frac1{12}\int_a^b\frac{f(x)}{g(x)^2}\,dx.$$

This is an exact limit for the specified compact construction. It assumes neither an unbounded source nor negligible overload, and it makes no claim about unrestricted optimal quantizers or dimensions greater than one.
thm-it-optimal-compact-compander-density:
## Statement

Fix $a<b$ and a positive normalized $C^1$ source density $f$ on $[a,b]$. Among all positive normalized $C^1$ point densities $g$ used in [[def-it-compact-one-dimensional-compander]], the asymptotic coefficient from [[thm-it-compact-compander-high-rate-distortion]] is uniquely minimized by

$$g_*(x)=\frac{f(x)^{1/3}}{\int_a^bf(t)^{1/3}\,dt},$$

and the minimum limit is

$$\frac1{12}\left(\int_a^bf(x)^{1/3}\,dx\right)^3.$$

This is optimality within the stated compact compander class, not unrestricted scalar or vector quantizer optimality.
